calls.head: Top line on top line: Suzuki against Benson
calls.body: At home, the Canadiens keep sending Suzuki’s line (Suzuki, Caufield and Slafkovský) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Martin St. Louis has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Quinn, Östlund and Benson.

calls.head: Where the Sabres have the edge: preventing dangerous shots
calls.body: The Sabres are around the middle of the league for preventing dangerous shots, and the Canadiens are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Sabres prevent dangerous shots better than the Canadiens do.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Caufield wins it in overtime
paras: Josh Norris got the scoring started for the Sabres midway through the first. Zachary Bolduc and Cole Caufield scored a little over two minutes apart later in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Alexandre Texier made it 3-1 midway through the second, but Jack Quinn cut Montréal’s lead to 3-2 shorthanded a little over two minutes later. Tage Thompson tied it 3-3 midway through the third. Caufield won it with his second goal of the night 54 seconds into overtime.
Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Jacob Fowler made 23 saves for the Canadiens, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 30 of 34.
The Canadiens killed all four Sabres power plays. The Habs moved to 4-3-1, and the Sabres dropped to 4-3-2.

items.text: Tage Thompson passed Jason Pominville for tenth on the Sabres’ all-time goals list, with 218.
Nick Suzuki extended his point streak against Buffalo to ten games.
Alexandre Texier scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 11 (18 games played since).
The Canadiens have won both meetings this season.
